findings.detail: The workflow runs on any pushed `desktop-v*` tag and on `workflow_dispatch` from any branch. Nothing checks that the tagged commit is reachable from master or that the run uses a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers. The job imports the shared Eigen Labs Developer ID p12 and Apple notarization credentials, then publishes (tag) or uploads (dispatch) a Developer-ID-signed, notarized app. Anyone able to push a tag or branch can get arbitrary code built, signed and notarized under the vendor identity that also signs the CLI. Dispatch from a modified branch yields a signed artifact even without a release. Fix: bind the secrets to a protected environment, restrict the tag/branch to master (e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor $GITHUB_SHA origin/master`), and use tag protection rules.
findings.title: Release signing/notarization secrets are reachable from any ref; tag or dispatch is not tied to a protected branch or environment

findings.detail: The Developer ID key is imported into an unlocked keychain on the user search list (lines 94-109) before dependencies are installed. The next step then runs `npm ci`, which executes dependency lifecycle scripts, with `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD` and `APPLE_ID` in its environment (lines 125-130). A compromised or typosquatted npm package could use `codesign`/`security` to sign arbitrary binaries as team SLDQ2GJ6TL, or read the notarization password. Fix: install dependencies in an earlier step before the cert import and without secrets (`npm ci --ignore-scripts`, running only trusted rebuilds), and expose the Apple credentials only to the packaging and notarize commands.
findings.title: `npm ci` runs with an unlocked Developer ID keychain and notarization password in its environment

findings.detail: `cli` comes from `curl` on api.darkbloom.dev/v1/releases/latest and is echoed into `$GITHUB_ENV` without validation. This happens unconditionally on the dry-run branch (line 81), and on the success branch only after the `git cat-file` check. A response with an embedded newline could inject arbitrary environment variables (e.g. NODE_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV, PUBLISH, CSC_NAME) into later steps that hold the signing key. This extends CI signing trust to the coordinator's HTTP response. Fix: validate the value against a strict semver regex before using or exporting it.
findings.title: Unvalidated coordinator API version string is written to GITHUB_ENV

findings.detail: The workflow runs on any pushed `desktop-v*` tag and on `workflow_dispatch` from any ref (lines 14-17). Nothing in the supplied file requires the commit to be reachable from master, and no protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers is used. The job imports the shared Eigen Labs Developer ID p12 and the Apple notarization credentials (lines 83-117, 124-125). A user who can push a tag or a branch can get arbitrary code built, signed and notarized under the vendor identity that also signs the CLI. Tag runs also publish a GitHub Release. Dispatch runs from a modified branch yield a signed artifact. Fix: bind the secrets to a protected environment, verify that `$GITHUB_SHA` is an ancestor of origin/master, and add tag protection rules. Repository-level protections are outside the supplied evidence.
findings.title: Developer ID signing and notarization secrets are reachable from any pushed desktop-v* tag or any-branch workflow_dispatch

findings.detail: The Developer ID key is imported into an unlocked keychain on the user search list (lines 94-108). The next step then runs `npm ci` (line 128) with `APPLE_ID` and `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD` in its environment (lines 124-125). A compromised dependency lifecycle script could sign arbitrary binaries as team SLDQ2GJ6TL or read the notarization password. The packaging step must run the same dependency tree with these secrets anyway, so the extra exposure is limited to install-time scripts. Fix: install dependencies in an earlier step, before the cert import and without secrets, using `npm ci --ignore-scripts` plus explicit trusted rebuilds. Expose the Apple credentials only to the packaging and notarize commands.
findings.title: `npm ci` lifecycle scripts run while the Developer ID keychain is unlocked and Apple credentials are in the environment

findings.detail: `cli` comes from `curl` on api.darkbloom.dev/v1/releases/latest and is written to `$GITHUB_ENV` without validation. This happens on the dry-run branch (line 80) and on the success branch (line 74). If the response were malformed or compromised, a value containing newlines could inject environment variables such as NODE_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV or CSC_NAME into later steps that hold the signing key. The coordinator is trusted in this model, so exploitation needs an upstream compromise. Fix: validate the value against a strict semver regex before using or exporting it.
findings.title: Unvalidated CLI version string from the release API is written to GITHUB_ENV
